title: Asymptotes of Rational Functions
seo_title: Precalculus Asymptotes of Rational Functions Worksheets (TEKS P.2K)
standard_text: P.2K analyze characteristics of rational functions and the behavior of the function around the asymptotes, including horizontal, vertical, and oblique asymptotes
meta_desc: Free Precalculus worksheets on rational function asymptotes for Texas TEKS P.2K: horizontal, vertical and slant asymptotes, behavior near asymptotes and graphs. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Slant asymptote: divide and keep the quotient.
key_sub: Check the sign of the fraction on each side of a vertical asymptote.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Vertical asymptote: a zero of the denominator that does not cancel.
  • Horizontal asymptote: bottom degree bigger → y = 0; equal degrees → ratio of leading coefficients.
  • Slant (oblique) asymptote: when the top degree is one more than the bottom, divide; the quotient (without the remainder) is the asymptote.
  • Near a vertical asymptote, check the sign of the fraction on each side: it goes to ∞ or −∞.

Examples

Example

f(x) = x2 + 3x + 1x − 1

Quotient x + 4, remainder 5

Answer: Slant asymptote y = x + 4

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Keeping the remainderThe asymptote is the quotient only.
Using the ratio for a slant asymptoteThat rule is only for equal degrees.
The wrong sign on one sideTest a value just left and just right.

items.q: What is the slant asymptote of f(x) = x² + x + 7x + 2?
items.e: The numerator's degree is one more than the denominator's, so divide: (x² + x + 7) ÷ (x + 2) = x − 1 with remainder 9. The slant asymptote is y = x − 1.

items.q: What is the horizontal asymptote of f(x) = 5x − 3x² − 4?

items.e: The horizontal asymptote is y = 12 ÷ 1 = 12: the setup cost is shared by more and more posters. $12.
